A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same local-routing-consistency study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated SRP definitions and supplementary analyses.

before.justification: v2 reports original routing analyses across 20 MoE models, cache-algorithm comparisons, and appendix results on specialization, post-training, and statistical uncertainty.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical analyses and adds pretrained toy-model experiments, optimal-cache comparisons, and measured offloading-overhead results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The computation of SCH, one of the two proposed measures, changes substantially. v2 optimizes an expert set held fixed throughout each segment; v3 simulates token-by-token loading and eviction, removing unused experts with the lowest activation frequency over the next m tokens. SRP's underlying optimization remains unchanged.

E1.justification: The same 11-domain evaluation corpus is retained; changing '7' to '11' in Section 4.1 corrects the description rather than adding domains. v3 additionally uses a 20B-token sample of OLMoE pretraining data and evaluates actual offloading during prefilling and decoding in Appendix F.

E2.justification: v3 adds clairvoyant optimal replacement as the reference for the new Table 4 comparison of SCH, LRU, and LFU. Table 3 retains all three earlier comparator columns—LRU, LFU, and Fixed—even though v3's accompanying prose and caption describe only LRU and LFU.

E3.justification: v3 introduces controlled pretraining experiments across ten approximately 1.43B-parameter toy configurations, varying expert counts, activation counts, shared experts, dense-layer placement, and load-balancing loss. It also adds optimal-hit-rate normalization and separate prefilling/decoding overhead measurements against full-GPU inference. SCH's evaluation procedure changes, while the original 22,528 evaluation sequences of 512 tokens are retained.

E4.justification: Section 3.3 adds interventions testing which architectural and training factors affect consistency, and Appendix F tests its relationship to system overhead. v2's dedicated real-model perplexity and broader architecture analyses in Appendices E.2–E.3 are removed. Most earlier post-training, position, domain, layer, and expert analyses are retained under new numbering.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% SCH confidence intervals obtained from 1,000 bootstrap resamples and retain the deterministic-configuration statement. No changed repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported. Different confidence-interval values belong to the changed results.

E6.justification: v3 Table 2 adds toy-model SRPs, including Baseline 43.56, NoLB 56.42, and OverLB 36.42. SCH curves and Tables 7–8 change under the revised metric; for example, Table 7's correlation at m=16 and rho=2 changes from 98.49 to 94.87, without establishing a same-metric performance loss. Table 4 adds optimal-relative hit rates, and Appendix F reports SCH correlations with relative overhead of approximately +0.2 during prefilling and -0.3 during decoding. The earlier real-model perplexity plot is removed.

T1.justification: v2's fixed-segment SCH maximization and derivation in Equations 8–9 are replaced by a different operational definition, explicitly distinguished from clairvoyant optimal replacement. Appendix F adds an informal overhead argument under ideal-prefetching and memory assumptions. The SRP definitions and proofs are substantially preserved and relocated to Appendix C.

C1.justification: v2 foregrounds the finding that models with MoE in every layer and no shared experts have the highest consistency. v3's abstract, contributions, and conclusion instead emphasize toy-model verification of local load-balance tradeoffs, coexistence with global balance, and expert-combination space. The domain-versus-vocabulary specialization and approximately two-times-cache recommendations remain.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies v2's speculation that dense components weaken routing: interleaved dense layers show little direct effect, and other factors may explain the earlier association. It adds shared-expert bypass and combination-space explanations, distinguishes local from global load balance, and suggests a pretraining-data explanation for domain patterns. Appendix F explicitly limits throughput implications because measured overhead correlations are weak and implementation factors also matter.

D1.justification: New Appendix D.2 documents toy architectures and training settings, including the eight-layer, 1,280-dimensional baseline, expert configurations, 10,000 steps, sequence length 4,096, batch size 1,024, and learning-rate schedule. Appendix F describes the LRU/on-demand implementation. Conversely, v2's disclosure of eight RTX 4090 GPUs and BF16 precision disappears. Evaluation-data preparation and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Appendix B are unchanged. Positioning is modestly extended through comparison with clairvoyant optimal replacement and attribution of the expert-combination-space explanation to the already cited Muennighoff et al. (2025).

P1.justification: Section 2 replaces much of its mathematical exposition with explanatory prose and moves formal SRP material to Appendix C. Section 3.3 is extensively rewritten around the REAL/TOY distinction and individual factors. The headline narrative, appendix organization, and throughput discussion are substantially reworked.

P2.justification: v3 adds SRP/SCH illustrations, a toy-model scatterplot, expanded Table 2, and new Table 4. The main SRP and specialization plots change from horizontal four-panel displays to two-by-two arrangements. Earlier real-model perplexity and architecture-comparison displays are removed, while many retained appendix figures receive revised labels, captions, placement, and SCH curves.

improvement.justification: v2's architecture recommendations relied on comparisons among heterogeneous pretrained models. v3 substantially strengthens their evidential basis with controlled toy-model interventions and uses those results to qualify the dense-layer claim. Appendix F also tests the connection to system performance and acknowledges its weak correlations. These improve support and claim calibration despite reporting drawbacks, including removed hardware/precision details and Table 8 populating a SwitchTransformers decoder m=256 entry that its caption still calls invalid.
